name_en: Imobota — a taro-and-rice mochi wrapped around sweet red bean paste
summary_ja: うるち米に里芋を炊き込んでつぶし、小豆あんで包んだ奈良のぼた餅。もち米が貴重だった頃、里芋の粘りでもち米のような食感を出したとされ、収穫を終えた十一月の亥の日に仏壇へ供える地域が多い。
summary_en: A Nara-style sweet rice cake made by cooking taro into non-glutinous rice, mashing it, and wrapping it around sweet red bean paste. When glutinous rice was precious, taro's own stickiness is said to have stood in for it, and in many areas it is offered at the household altar on the Day of the Boar in November, once the harvest is in.
source_publisher: 農林水産省「うちの郷土料理」

name_ja: 半夏生餅／小麦餅／さなぶり餅
name_en: Hangesho mochi — cracked wheat pounded with glutinous rice, made at the close of rice planting
summary_ja: 夏至から十一日目の「半夏生」の頃、つぶし小麦ともち米をついて作る奈良盆地の餅。小麦の収穫と田植えが一段落する節目に作られ、田の神を送る早苗饗の行事に合わせて食べることから「さなぶり餅」とも呼ばれる。
summary_en: A Nara Basin mochi pounded from cracked wheat and glutinous rice around hangesho, the eleventh day after the summer solstice. It is made at the point when the wheat harvest and rice planting both wind down, and is also called sanaburi mochi for the rite that sends off the rice-field deity.
source_title: 半夏生餅／小麦餅／さなぶり餅
source_publisher: 農林水産省「うちの郷土料理」

name_en: Yoshino kuzumochi — a jelly-like cake made from Yoshino arrowroot starch
summary_ja: 吉野本葛を水と砂糖で溶き、透明になるまで練り上げた奈良の餅菓子。厳冬期の地下水にさらして精製する吉野晒しの製法で作られ、きなこや黒蜜をかけて、冷やしても作りたてのほんのり温かさが残っていても味わえる。
summary_en: A Nara sweet made by dissolving Yoshino arrowroot starch in water and sugar and stirring it over heat until translucent. It is refined through the Yoshino-zarashi method, repeated rinsing in midwinter groundwater, and is eaten with soybean flour or dark syrup, whether chilled firm or still faintly warm from the pan.
source_publisher: 農林水産省「うちの郷土料理」

name_en: Warabi mochi — a soft jelly-like sweet made from bracken-root starch
summary_ja: 蕨粉に水と砂糖を加えて練り、冷やし固めた奈良の和菓子。若草山焼きのあと山肌に群生したワラビが蕨粉の産地となったと伝わり、江戸期の紀行文にも山焼き後の茶屋で扱われていたことが記されているという。
summary_en: A Nara sweet made by cooking bracken-root starch with water and sugar into a soft, chilled jelly. Bracken is said to have grown thick on the hillside after the annual burning of Mount Wakakusa, making the area a source of the starch, and an Edo-period travel account already names it a specialty of teahouses there.
source_publisher: 農林水産省「うちの郷土料理」

name_en: Kakigori — shaved ice, a summer sweet with roots in Nara's ice-worship shrine
summary_ja: 削った氷にシロップをかけて食べる奈良の夏の菓子。奈良市の氷室神社では約七十年にわたり氷を宮中へ献上したと伝わり、清少納言も削り氷に甘葛をかけて食べたと枕草子に記しているとされる。
summary_en: Shaved ice topped with syrup, a summer sweet in Nara. Nara City's Himuro Shrine is said to have sent ice to the imperial court for roughly seventy years, and Sei Shonagon is said to describe shaved ice sweetened with amazura sap in the Pillow Book.
source_publisher: 農林水産省「うちの郷土料理」

name_en: Dengara — a bean-paste rice cake wrapped in magnolia leaves for Boys' Day
summary_ja: 餡を包んだ餅を朴の葉でくるんで蒸す東吉野村・川上村の菓子。男の子の立身出世や無事な成長を願う端午の節句に作られ、一本の枝から出た葉ひとつひとつに餅を包むため、房のような形になるという。
summary_en: A sweet from Higashiyoshino and Kawakami villages: bean-paste mochi steamed inside magnolia leaves. It is made for Boys' Day, wishing a son success and safe growth, and because each leaf on a single branch is wrapped around its own mochi, the finished cluster hangs like a bunch of fruit.
source_publisher: 農林水産省「うちの郷土料理」

name_en: Shikishiki — a thin wheat-flour griddle cake folded around sweet pea paste
summary_ja: 小麦粉を水と砂糖で溶いて薄く焼く、戦前からある奈良のおやつ。えんどう豆のあんを挟んで折りたたむのが定番で、小麦栽培が盛んだった奈良では三輪素麺や半夏生餅と並ぶ小麦文化の一つとされている。
summary_en: A prewar Nara snack made by thinning wheat flour with water and sugar and frying it thin like a crepe. It is usually folded around a filling of sweetened pea paste, and is counted alongside Miwa somen and hangesho mochi as part of Nara's wheat-growing food culture.
source_publisher: 農林水産省「うちの郷土料理」
